summary: Headline-level framing across the cluster is mostly feature or solution: the insights index catalogues "reasoning methods used in the programme", the three thinking articles open on what the method fixes, the exec-ed-vs-EMBA guide compares credential/duration/assessment, and /resources lists details. The two pages already built on the owner's lens are /insights/advancement-question (its spine is the RJTBD question "Which consequential work must I become better able to examine, explain and lead?") and /resources/advancement-brief (H1 "Is your role growing faster than your management toolkit?", chapter "03 / What changes": "A current business issue becomes a structured action plan."). RJTBD language also appears verbatim in the design-thinking article (the bank customer "hiring a service to answer one anxious question") and the /resources checklist ("What work must this learning help me do more effectively?"). Servant leadership is present but unnamed: design thinking "begin with the person you are trying to serve", systems thinking replacing "who is responsible?" with "what structure makes this failure the natural result?", and /resources serving before asking ("no contact details required", "No score or data submission is required"). The Service rung is absent from every CTA; CTAs are process labels ("Read →", "Explore the programme", "Get the free 2026 programme guide", "Send my programme request →"). Hope appears in both thinking articles ("none of this is innate") but is buried at the end. "Shortcut cuts" already exists as method critique (benchmarking caps you, quality cuts churn later, sticky-note workshops) and must stay aimed at methods, never at providers or the 18–24 month academic MBA. Governance collisions found while mapping, independent of the framework: (1) /resources employer guide uses "certificate-phase schedule", retired 3+3 wording that evades the audit regex only because of the hyphen; (2) undefined norms "normally" (exec-ed table) and "frequently" (first-principles example) are not in the regex but breach the clarity standard; (3) LeadForm intent "I am applying from outside Malaysia." uses "applying" against the enquiry-not-application rule; (4) CTA_LABELS.guide "Get the free 2026 programme guide" names no purpose, routes to /apply, and sits on /resources/advancement-brief, which is itself the guide; (5) /resources CTA "Understand the pathway" for Chartered Manager risks implying a fixed second stage; (6) outcome-adjacent phrasing in the thinking articles ("builds the habit until it becomes instinct", "becomes an instinct", "From method to mastery", "a programme built to move leaders..."). Any progress/experience rewrite must describe practice (applied project, coaching, sessions) rather than results, keep the CMI/MQA/fee/scholarship/HRD Corp sentences verbatim, and avoid the audit's aspiration list (unlock/elevate/redefine/reimagine/empower your, game-changing, future-proof).

summary: The English copy in this cluster is honest, exact and low-pressure (it already passes the governance bar), but it frames the offer mostly as FEATURE (what the programme has: 6 months, 6 days, 12 modules, CMI, cohorts) and SOLUTION/DECISION-SUPPORT (guide, checklist, facts to verify). PROGRESS/HOPE appears once, in the hero headline ("Your next leadership chapter starts here."), and then the lede immediately reverts to a product description. CHANGE OF EXPERIENCE is present but buried: the audience points ("Bring a current business issue. / Learn through a rigorous structure that fits around work. / Leave with a practical plan you can explain, test and act on."), the experience section ("A working room built around real decisions.") and the diagnostic Q2 options are the strongest before-to-after lines on the site. The RJTBD is latent in two sentences: "1 · built around a live business challenge" and the diagnostic card "The useful test is whether the work can address a real organisational question." The SERVICE rung of 5S exists in one line only: "For people whose decisions affect more than their own desk." The diagnostic is JTBD-shaped (why now / where would structure help) but its result is a static, feature-only checklist that does not reflect the reader's chosen state back. Naming drift undermines the "one thing" principle: the guide is called "free 2026 guide", "free 2026 programme guide", "Future Ready EMBA guide", "private decision guide", "The Working Manager's 2026 Progression Guide", "advancement brief" and, in the confirmation email, "programme plan"; the diagnostic is "Programme fit check" in NAV, "Working Manager Progression Check" in metadata and "Your private review checklist" on the result. Biggest framework levers, all compatible with governance: (1) name the reader's from-state and to-state in their own working life (decisions they will make differently, people who depend on them) without any career/salary/promotion outcome; (2) make the applied project on a real business issue the centre (RJTBD) and let CMI recognition, cohort counts and HRD Corp be supporting proof (right over good); (3) carry the reader's chosen state through the funnel (diagnostic answers -> result -> guide -> success screen -> email) and honour a "details first, no call" choice in success and email copy; (4) settle one name for the guide and one for the check; (5) turn FORCES from fear ("Competitors are adapting faster than you") to hope; (6) keep "six months, no thesis" as the right-sized route for a working manager, never as a shortcut, and keep the comparison table's academic MBA column neutral. Governance collisions to watch: the home page shows a gown-and-cap hero, "awarded and endorsed", "graduates" and "graduation" without the "not an MQA-accredited academic degree" boundary anywhere in its English body; "deserving comes out of serving" must never touch the scholarship (selective, individual, written, no amounts, no new criteria); "progression" naming edges toward career-outcome framing; the /apply route name sits under an "Arrange a programme conversation" label; and the email subject "We've received your programme conversation request" mislabels guide-only requests.

A structured action plan leaves." and "Reuse the method", meta LP's "Why managers begin looking" pressures, entrepreneurs' "From proposition to an executable business model". cluster: Trust, funding and recognition support pages (EN): HRD Corp, CMI recognition, provider, coordinator, FAQ, comparison table, progression chart, two legacy redirects, plus the shared enquiry block they all render
summary: This cluster is the site's verification layer, and its copy is deliberately feature/solution-framed: bodies, processes, boundaries and who-decides-what. That is correct under governance, but it means the reader's progress (the change in how they decide at work) is almost never the headline. The cluster already owns two authentic progress lines that can be reused as models: /about ("progress is rarely a straight line. It comes from learning to see the situation clearly, make the next sound decision and keep moving.") and /chartered-manager-malaysia ("Bring one real decision. Leave with a stronger way to make the next one."). Largest opportunities: (1) /hrd-corp-claimable H1, 'What's covered' and CTA are process/paperwork-framed with no employer progress; (2) /asian-business-consulting is provenance-framed ('the firm behind') and contains a clarity-standard breach ('over almost three years of development with CMI') and a 'partners' implication; (3) ProgrammeComparison's 'us' column carries shortcut cues (no exam/thesis, while working) on the surface where 'shortcut cuts' collides hardest with the no-disparagement rule; (4) /faq has no question about what changes for the participant; (5) the shared CtaSection default 'Get the facts you need to decide.' serves facts, not the decision; (6) CmiProgressionChart is dormant (no route imports it) yet still audit-scanned. Recurring governance collisions to police: hope/progress must never become outcome promises (promotion, salary, business results, board-ready); 5S Safety must never become 'risk-free' or automatic funding; 'shortcut cuts' must never rank other providers, academic MBAs or attendance certificates ('not another attendance certificate' on the chartered page is already adjacent to the banned 'certificate on a shelf'); every fact string lives in src/lib/content.ts with zh/ms mirrors and FAQPage JSON-LD, so framework rewrites must land there, not in pages. Two redirect files carry no copy but raise RJTBD questions about where a 'corporate training' or 'shift-hr' searcher should land, and the audit still carves out /programmes/shift-hr from the 'HRD Corp claimable' sentence check. All paths below are absolute; line numbers refer to the file as read on 2026-09-07.

claimsToProtect: Q: How is the programme structured? — The Executive MBA runs for 6 months. Participants complete 6 training days across 3 scheduled sessions, receive coaching and complete an applied business project leading to the CMI-recognised Executive MBA programme certificate. Chartered Manager is a separate optional CMI route with its own eligibility, assessment and fees; it is not included in the published Executive MBA programme or fee.

Q: Can I complete the programme while working full time? — Yes. The Malaysian public programme runs across 3 scheduled sessions, with 6 scheduled training days in total. Participants remain in their professional roles and complete an applied project based on a current business issue. Review every published session date before enrolling.

Q: Is this executive education or an academic MBA degree? — The Executive MBA on Future Ready Business Leadership is awarded and endorsed by CMI. It is a six-month professional development and executive education programme, not an MQA-accredited academic degree or a regulated qualification.

Q: What do successful participants receive? — Successful participants receive the CMI Certificate of Recognition for the Future Ready Executive MBA programme. CMI controls the final certificate format and wording. Chartered Manager is a separate CMI route and is not automatically awarded through programme completion.

Q: Does completing the programme make me a Chartered Manager? — No. Successful programme completion leads to the CMI Certificate of Recognition and, under CMI's published CMI Recognised offer, Foundation Chartered Manager status. Full Chartered Manager status is separate. CMI determines the participant's route and eligibility, assesses the application and professional evidence, and controls the award, membership and fees.

summary:
Read in full: SEO-CONTENT-GOVERNANCE.md, content-clarity-audit.mjs (banned patterns + file scope), the ten listed files, and the content.ts constants they interpolate (CTA_LABELS, NAV, FACTS, HRD_CORP_CLAIM, PROGRAMME_POSITIONING_SENTENCE, OPERATOR, SITE, CERTIFICATE_POSITIONING). 17 copy units mapped.

FRAME FINDING. The cluster is overwhelmingly FEATURE-framed (what the programme has, what the guide contains, what the team will send) sitting on a strong, well-executed 5S SAFETY rung (no payment, not admission, confirmed in writing, PDPA, named coordinator). That Safety layer is the trust asset and must survive any rewrite. PROGRESS/HOPE appears in only three places: the decision-guide PDF cover ("Made for the decision you're facing now." / "the responsibility you already carry — not just the title you would like next."), LeadForm step 1 ("What are you planning for?") and CtaSection ("Get the facts you need to decide."). CHANGE OF EXPERIENCE is documented factually but buried: "the applied work happens inside your business between sessions" (day7), "Judgment on your own live business issue" (decision-guide table), "define a problem, weigh options and turn a decision into an action plan" (decision-guide method card). These evidence-backed activity descriptions are the only permissible raw material for experience framing, because governance bans outcome framing (promotion, board-ready, future-proof). RIGHT-VS-GOOD seeds exist: "The calendar decides more than the brochure does", "The outcome is applied, not just attendance", "Clear terms protect everyone", "not just the title you would like next", and the chatbot Comparison rule. SERVANT LEADERSHIP shows only as mechanics ("the team reads every reply", "tell the team before you rule it out", "Decide your next step after receiving the information", Roy Affandi named) — never as a stated posture. 5S: Survival n/a; Safety strong; Social absent (no cohort/peer copy in this cluster); Success present as "Career progression" intent label and PROGRAMME_AUDIENCE; SERVICE rung absent except implicitly in the employer brief — the largest untapped lever, usable only via "responsibility for people" language, never results.

GOVERNANCE BREACHES FOUND (current copy, not framework proposals): (1) nurture day3 "Most readers tell us three sections decide it for them" — banned norm "most" and an unsupported participant claim under the evidence standard; (2) nurture day7 "the calendar conversation is usually the shortest one" — banned "usually"; (3) nurture day3/day7 "3 scheduled weekends" / "3 weekend sessions" / "no time out of the business" — fact drift against chat-knowledge.ts attendance fact (only English Cohort 17 is Sat–Sun; other cohorts Fri–Sat); (4) en.json decision-guide table "Typically 18–24 months" — banned "typically", COMPARISON_SCOPE gives the exact figure; (5) en.json employer-funding-brief kicker "EMPLOYER DECISION BRIEF" matches banned "decision brief", and promise "questions a sponsor usually asks" — banned "usually"; (6) en.json working-managers-guide CTA "Request the programme guide or arrange a conversation" matches the retired CTA pattern "Request the programme guide" and is circular inside the guide; (7) llms.txt "[Apply]: the enrolment enquiry form" conflates the controlled terms enrolment/enquiry; (8) employer brief notice "authorised programme partner" departs from the controlled role "marketing agency". Borderline: "One conversation. No commitment." / "no follow-up pressure" (day14), "no-obligation" (decision guide) sit beside the banned "no-pressure enquiry" device and the banned ZH 无需承诺; "private decision guide" (LeadForm campaign helper, decision-guide kicker) sits beside banned "private decision tool" and adds a third name for the same PDF ("programme guide", "Working Manager's Guide", "programme plan"). Root cause: src/lib/nurture-email.ts and scripts/pdf/copy/*.json are NOT in content-clarity-audit.mjs's file list, so npm run audit:content never sees them — recommend adding both before any rewrite.

FRAMEWORK/GOVERNANCE COLLISION RULES for the rewrite: "sometimes the shortcut cuts" may only be expressed as a difference in purpose and documentation between routes (as COMPARISON_SCOPE and the chatbot Comparison rule already do), never as a judgement on HRD Corp providers, attendance-only training or academic MBAs; "progress" must be described as what the participant does during the six months (activities, decision processes, the applied project in their own business), never what happens to their career after; "hope" must not become urgency (no seat counts, countdowns, "remaining" beyond the factual calendar); "deserving through serving" may describe the team's posture (serve answers first, the reader decides, "no" is a valid outcome) but never the scholarship, where it would read as selection criteria; Service-rung wording may reference responsibility for people but not organisational outcomes or ROI. Every new sentence must be sourced from content.ts constants (governance: pages, emails, chatbot and llms.txt reuse facts, never independent versions).
